title: How to automate invoice reminders (any tool) | 50agents
description: Automate invoice reminders in four parts: one list of open invoices, a rule for who is due a nudge, a message per stage, and a stop the moment money lands.
answer: Keep one list of open invoices with a due date and status, and email only those sent, unpaid and past due.
If every invoice sits in one accounting app, use its reminders; if not, an automation or AI agent.

then.q: Do you want to read each reminder before it goes?

then.answer: Switch on your accounting app's reminders
then.why: It sees each payment as it is recorded, so it stops chasing on its own. QuickBooks, Xero and Zoho Books all have them.

options.label: Yes, I want to check each one

then.why: Built-in reminders send on their own. An AI agent that drafts each email and waits for your yes lets you hold one for a client who just called.
Stripe marks an invoice paid itself when the money clears, so its reminders stop at the right moment.

then.answer: Use an automation or an AI agent on one list
then.why: Something has to read your list every day. Follow the steps below, and keep the Paid column true.

sections.h2: The four parts every reminder setup needs

head: Part
What it is
The usual mistake
rows: Every open invoice, with a status
Paid status the tool cannot see
Sent, unpaid, past due, not on hold
One template for day 1 and day 45
Paid, a promise, or a dispute

body.p: The stop matters most. A reminder to someone who has already paid costs more goodwill than a late reminder ever would.

steps.title: Make one list of open invoices
steps.body: Export open invoices to one sheet or table. Columns: invoice number, client, client email, amount, currency, due date, status. One row per invoice, never one per client.

steps.title: Write the rule in one sentence
steps.body: For example: "status is Sent, due date is before today, and no reminder went in the last 6 days". Make exceptions statuses (Disputed, On a plan), not notes, so the tool can read them.

steps.title: Set the stages and the gaps
steps.body: A first nudge a day or two after the due date, then one every week or two, firmer each time, then a final notice. Write the stage on the invoice when a reminder goes.

note.text: If your accounting app's reminders are on, switch them off for these invoices. Two tools chasing one client is the most common mistake.

steps.title: Write one email per stage
steps.body: Subject with the invoice number and amount. Two or three lines: what is due, since when, how to pay, and a question that asks for a date. A payment link beats a PDF.

steps.title: Test on yourself, from your own address
steps.body: Send from the inbox you read, so replies come back to you. Run it once with your own email as the client and check every field fills in, currency included.

steps.title: Close the loop every day
steps.body: Mark invoices Paid as money arrives, before the reminders run. Then skim what went out this week; a quick read catches a wrong amount before a client does.

note.text: Run reminders at a fixed time each morning, after you have marked the day's payments, so nobody is chased minutes after paying.

captain.line: Captain builds an invoices desk: your list, a Late view, and an AI agent that drafts each stage's email and waits for your yes before it sends.

wrong.title: A client gets chased after paying
wrong.body: The payment landed after the tool read the list. Mark payments before the daily run, and keep the gap between the read and the send short.

wrong.title: Invoices never emailed get no reminder
wrong.body: QuickBooks only reminds on invoices sent from QuickBooks, so PDFs sent from your own mail are skipped. Use a list-based tool for those.

wrong.title: Partial payments read as unpaid
wrong.body: A client pays half and still gets a full reminder. Add a Part paid status and an amount still due, and quote that amount in the email.

wrong.title: The wrong currency or amount
wrong.body: Imports can turn 1.250,00 into 1.25 or drop the currency. Check a few rows after every import, and send one test to yourself first.

wrong.title: A drafted reminder sounds wrong
wrong.body: An AI agent can be too firm with a good client. Read drafts before they go for the first few weeks, and tell it the tone you want per stage.

faqs.q: Is it rude to send automatic payment reminders?
faqs.a: Not when they read like a person wrote them: short, specific, and polite on the first one. Clients forget invoices far more often than they refuse them, and a clear reminder with a payment link is a help.

faqs.q: Should the reminder include the invoice PDF?
faqs.a: A link to pay or view the invoice is better, because a link always shows the current amount. If you cannot attach the current PDF, leave it out and quote the number and amount in the subject.

faqs.q: Can I automate reminders without an accounting app?
faqs.a: Yes. A spreadsheet with a Status column is enough for an automation or an AI agent to read each day. The cost is that you keep Paid up to date by hand.
